what: The Ideal Weight Calculator estimates an ideal body weight from your height and sex using four well-known formulas: Devine, Robinson, Miller and Hamwi. It also shows the average of the four, the range between them, and the weight range that gives a healthy BMI of 18.5 to 24.9 for your height.
These formulas were first made for working out medicine doses and only look at height and sex, so they are a rough guide. The healthy BMI range is often more useful as a target.
Results are calculated in your browser in kg or lb. This is not medical advice; talk to a doctor about your weight.
uses: See a realistic target range for your height.
See how four classic formulas differ for the same height.
Find the weights that give a BMI from 18.5 to 24.9.
Nurses and students can check the Devine formula used in dose calculations.
Work in cm and kg or feet, inches and pounds.
tutorial: Pick "Metric (kg, cm)" or "Imperial (lb, ft, in)" in "Units".
The formulas use different numbers for men and women.
Type your height in cm, or in feet and inches in the two boxes.
The boxes show the average of the four formulas, the range from the lowest to the highest, and the healthy BMI range.
The table lists the result from each formula, in kg or lb.
features: Men 50 kg + 2.3 kg per inch over 5 ft; women 45.5 kg + 2.3 kg per inch.
Men 52 kg + 1.9 kg per inch; women 49 kg + 1.7 kg per inch.
Men 56.2 kg + 1.41 kg per inch; women 53.1 kg + 1.36 kg per inch.
Men 48 kg + 2.7 kg per inch; women 45.5 kg + 2.2 kg per inch.
18.5 × height² to 24.9 × height², with height in metres.
Below 5 ft the formulas are extended downwards and a note warns that they are less reliable. Heights from 120 to 230 cm are accepted.

example.title: Worked example: a man 5 ft 10 in tall
example.text: 5 ft 10 in is 177.8 cm, 10 inches over 5 ft. Devine: 50 + 2.3 × 10 = 73.0 kg. Robinson: 52 + 1.9 × 10 = 71.0 kg. Miller: 56.2 + 1.41 × 10 = 70.3 kg. Hamwi: 48 + 2.7 × 10 = 75.0 kg. The average is 72.3 kg and the range 70.3 to 75.0 kg. The healthy BMI range for 1.778 m is 58.5 to 78.7 kg.

tips: Use the healthy BMI range as your main guide; the formulas are only one view.
Measure your height without shoes, standing straight against a wall.
Muscular people can be healthy above these numbers.
Small changes towards a healthy range matter more than hitting an exact number.
Ask a doctor before starting a big weight change.
problems: Enter your height. In imperial mode put feet in "Height (ft)" and the rest in "Height (in)".
It asks for a height between 120 and 230 cm
Check that you typed cm and not metres or inches.
That is normal. They were made from different data; the average and range give a fair picture.
There is a warning about 5 ft
The formulas were designed for people 5 ft or taller. Use the BMI range as a better guide.
